quotes.text: Machine learning is a program that finds patterns in examples. Instead of following rules, a person wrote by hand. That's the whole idea.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A plain-language definition of machine learning for beginners.

quotes.text: Every machine learning project needs the same three things, which are examples to learn from. A clear question to answer and compute to do the math.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Names the three prerequisites of any machine learning project.

quotes.text: The bigger idea here is that a machine learning project isn't a file you keep on a laptop. It's a living thing with versions, owners and a history
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why the workspace and run history matter.

quotes.text: You pay for the machines you switch on, billed by the second, plus the ordinary Azure services your project touches.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clarifies the cost model that beginners often misunderstand.

quotes.text: When it ships, the world keeps changing, the data keeps changing, and a model that was accurate last year can start missing the mark.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures why models drift and need ongoing operations.

chapters.title: Introduction: a workshop, not a robot

takeaways: Machine learning learns rules from examples, and every project needs examples, a clear question and compute.
Azure Machine Learning organizes work in a workspace that records every run, and you pay for the compute you switch on rather than for the platform itself.
Models can be built with notebooks, the designer or AutoML, served through online or batch endpoints, and kept accurate over time with MLOps pipelines.
hook: Many people assume machine learning needs a PhD and a big budget, so the data in their organization never answers a real question. This episode walks beginners and IT professionals through Azure Machine Learning piece by piece, from workspaces and compute to AutoML, endpoints and MLOps, so they can start with a question they already care about.
